subject: Class of 2020 Commencement Exercises
overview: Medford Public Schools held commencement exercises for the Class of 2020. School officials, student leaders, and guest speakers delivered addresses congratulating graduates and reflecting on their resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Staff Introductions
items.summary: Principal Paul D'Alleva introduced class officers, faculty advisors, and administrators, commending the graduating class for their perseverance through the pandemic.

items.title: Faculty Address
items.summary: Teacher Jonathan Brown delivered the faculty address, urging graduates to recognize their daily impact on others through small acts of kindness.

items.title: Class President Address
items.summary: Class of 2020 President Mark Allen Gene Mary reflected on high school memories, persistent social inequalities, and overcoming ongoing challenges.

items.title: Mayor's Address
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn acknowledged the disruption of the graduates' senior year and commended their determination, work ethic, and resilience.

items.title: Superintendent's Address
items.summary: Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent recognized graduates' achievements, urged adherence to public health guidance, and called on students to advocate for social justice.

items.title: Guest Commencement Address
items.summary: Former City Solicitor Mark Rumley offered advice to graduates on discarding negative messages and pursuing their passions.
